dedupe_keys.name: exadigit digital twin framework for liquid cooled supercomputers

description: ExaDigiT is an open-source framework for building digital twins of large liquid-cooled supercomputers and their data-centre plant. It has three modules: RAPS, the Resource Allocator and Power Simulator, which schedules synthetic workloads or replays job telemetry and estimates dynamic system power and conversion losses at set intervals; a transient thermo-fluid cooling model written in Modelica and run as a Functional Mock-up Unit, covering the path from cooling towers to cold plates and fed with power at the level of cooling distribution units; and a visual analytics layer in Unreal Engine 5 with augmented reality and a web dashboard. It was developed at Oak Ridge National Laboratory for the Frontier exascale system, described in an SC24 paper, and is used with partner centres; RAPS ships loaders for open telemetry of Marconi100 (CINECA) and Adastra (CINES) from Zenodo. Coverage: specific supercomputers and their cooling plants, with Frontier as the reference system and job traces from 2020 onward. Format and access: Python code (RAPS, Python 3.12 or later) on ORNL GitLab and GitHub with online documentation; free of charge, RAPS dual-licensed MIT or Apache 2.0. Caveats: configuring a new site needs detailed plant data; the cooling model is tailored to HPE Cray liquid cooling; visual modules need game-engine tools. Simulation uses: digital twin of data-centre power and cooling, capacity planning of power and plant upgrades, what-if tests of cooling failures and heat waves, and grid interaction of large computing loads. Related records: Sustain-LC uses its Frontier cooling model for control benchmarks, the Marconi100 ExaMon telemetry is a replay input, SustainDC is a lighter data-centre simulator.
